N1_fences_back_to_literal_lf._note:
The pre-#4453 plugin predicate. Every CRLF axis reddens on every surface; the BOM+LF cases stay green, and that asymmetry is what proves the two halves of the fix are separately load-bearing. X2 reddens because an unrecognised block is 'no block at all', so the malformed file is reported as an invariant violation instead of an unparseable-frontmatter skip — the silent-drop class #4439/#4440 closed. ⛤ C5 also reddens once it exists, and the reason is read rather than smoothed over: with an LF-only predicate `frontmatterBlockBody(CRLF)` is null, so C5 ends up comparing js-yaml's parse of nothing against the LF mapping. Same class as the other corrections in this PR (integration-test-revert-verify §A44) — the expectation had been written before C5 was added, from the mutant's theme rather than from which axes execute after it lands.
⚤ EXPECTATION WIDENED by req 74419202 (#4452), reason recorded rather than filled in silently (§A44): C6 is the axis #4452 added for the two shapes this predicate now reaches (lone-CR fences, a RUN of BOMs). Any mutant of the predicate's own half breaks it too — which is the point of ONE shared predicate, and the reason C6 lives in this spec's harness rather than in a separate one.
⚤ ANCHOR RE-MIGRATED (review round 2) — see the CLI twin M1.
⚤ EXPECTATION WIDENED AGAIN (review round 2 of #4452), reason first: C8 is the new control asserting that a genuinely EMPTY block (TWO separators) is recognised in ALL THREE encodings. Fences back to a literal `\n` breaks its CR row — `---\r\r---` stops being a block. So C8 belongs to the same half of the widening as C6 and reddens with it, which is what makes it a real pair for C7 rather than a restatement of it.

N3_predicate_loses_its_start_anchor._note:
Guards the OVER-WIDENING direction — the class #4439's review caught once already. Without `^`, a `---` fence inside the BODY is read as the asset's frontmatter, and the doubled-BOM file becomes visible through its SECOND fence. Narrow by construction: C4 is the only axis carrying shapes that must stay unrecognised.
⚤ `to` REPAIRED by req 74419202 (#4452) — the mutant, not the expectation. Its old `to` (`/---\r?\n…/`) dropped the anchor AND reverted the fences to `\r?\n` in one step, so after #4452 it was a MIXED mutant and reddened C6 for the SECOND reason (a lone-CR fence no longer matched at all) rather than for over-widening. Single-concern again: anchor only, three forms kept, expectation back to the over-widening control alone. The CLI twin M6 of `cli-frontmatter-predicate-unify-4461.core.spec.json` had the identical defect and the identical repair.
⚤ ANCHOR RE-MIGRATED (review round 2) — see the CLI twin M6.

N4_body_gets_its_carriage_returns_stripp._note:
The plausible 'helpful' normalisation, rejected on purpose: stripping would silently rewrite user content AND make the returned offsets stop matching the returned text. Narrow by construction — C2 is the only axis that asserts the body verbatim. ⛤ C5 added after the review of PR #4458: it asserts the same decision on a REAL YAML implementation (js-yaml) rather than on the hand-rolled Obsidian double, whose `\r` tolerance is incidental. N4 reddens both — C2 on the bytes, C5 on the parse.
⚤ ANCHOR RE-MIGRATED (review round 2): the body is now sliced out of the remainder rather than taken from a capture group, so the mutant strips `\r` from the slice. Same subject.

N5_offsets_ignore_the_bom._note: Keeps the BOM out of the MATCH but points the offsets at index 0, so a future write path splicing [blockStart, blockEnd) would eat the byte. Not reachable from today's read-only plugin call sites, which is exactly why it needs its own axis rather than relying on one.
